translationRepairs: (The 《Old Tales Heard among the Gentry of Luoyang》 says: The future Duke Sang of Wei's father Gong served as a Henan client officer. When the son was to sit for the examinations, the father found a moment to tell Wang Yun, "My boy has a measure of literary promise. His fellows are taking him to qualify for the provincial exam, and we await your word."

(The 《Old Tales Heard among the Gentry of Luoyang》 says: The future Duke Sang of Wei's father Gong served as a Henan client officer. When the son was to sit for the examinations, the father found a moment to tell the prince, saying, "My boy has a measure of literary promise. His fellows are taking him to qualify for the provincial exam, and we await your word."
The parallel source reads 告王曰, and the following sentence identifies that 王 as the Prince of Qi; 雲/云 is the quotative, not the personal name Wang Yun.
At that time the Tujue commander Bai Chengfu, harried by the Khitan, led his people to submit to the Jin court. Gaozu was courting the Khitan and refused to accept them.
At that time the Tuyuhun commander Bai Chengfu, harried by the Khitan, led his people to submit to the Jin court. Gaozu was courting the Khitan and refused to accept them.
吐渾 denotes the Tuyuhun, not the Turkic Tujue (突厥).

An Chongrong, governor of Zhenzhou, resented Khitan power and plotted attack. He secretly harmed troops passing through Zhending and had secretly allied with the Tujue; now he accepted them and sent them to court.

An Chongrong, governor of Zhenzhou, resented Khitan power and plotted attack. He secretly harmed troops passing through Zhending and had secretly allied with the Tuyuhun; now he accepted them and sent them to court.
The same group is explicitly 吐渾 in the surrounding passage.
Soon An Chongrong submitted a defiant memorial asking to attack the Khitan and citing the Tujue submission.
Soon An Chongrong submitted a defiant memorial asking to attack the Khitan and citing the Tuyuhun submission.
The memorial concerns the Tuyuhun petition, 吐渾之請.

Recently I have received successive reports from the Memorial Office: the Tujue leader Bai Chengfu has led his people to submit, and An Chongrong of Zhenzhou has memorialized for a campaign against the Khitan.

Recently I have received successive reports from the Memorial Office: the Tuyuhun leader Bai Chengfu has led his people to submit, and An Chongrong of Zhenzhou has memorialized for a campaign against the Khitan.
The later memorial repeats the correct ethnonym 吐渾.
and Emperor Taizu still styled himself subject to the qaghan.
and Tang Gaozu (Shenyao), despite his military prowess, still styled himself subject to the qaghan.
神堯 is the epithet/posthumous designation of Tang Gaozu Li Yuan, not Emperor Taizu; 武略 also supplies the military-prowess phrase.

At the time Du had a retainer named He Shaowei who had long envied Geng. He framed Geng and had him killed. Xu fled across the border and settled at Fuyang, where the military governor Li Cunshen recruited him as staff officer.

At the time Du had a retainer named He Shaowei who had long envied Xuan. He framed Xuan and had him killed. Xu fled across the border and settled at Fuyang, where the military governor Li Cunshen recruited him as staff officer.
Independent witnesses preserve 晅, Liu Xu's elder brother named in the preceding sentence; the 亙 graph is a textual corruption or variant, not a separate Geng.
